To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The water sorption behavior of different amorphous formulations can be predicted with PC SAFF, and 2) the water sorption behavior can be used to predict the phase behavior of formulations, including the glass transition temperatures, the API solubilities in the polymers, and the API crystallization behavior as a function of humidity.

water absorption in amorphous API/polymer systems can be predicted using the thermodynamic PC-SAFT model, which can be used to predict the effect of absorbed moisture on the glass transition and the phase behavior of the formulations, and thus to select appropriate API/poly-mer compositions for long term stable am-orphous formulations.

(i) water sorption in PVP and PVPVA based amorphous formulations is strongly affected by the presence of API; (ii) PC SAFT can accurately predict the water sorption in API/polymer systems; (iii) PC SAFT and Gordon Taylor equation can accurately predict the effect of water on the API solubilization and glass transition temperature of API/polymeric formulations, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a quantitative thermodynamic approach for the prediction of the phase behavior of amorphous API/polymer systems as a function of the relative humidity.
the development of a quantitative thermodynamic model to predict the influence of humidity on the stability of API/polyler formulations.
the influence of absorbed water on the phase behavior and stability of amorphous API/polymer systems, with the goal to predict and optimize their stability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
water absorption by the amorphous formulation is a major factor for API recrystalization.
the water sorption in API/polymer systems is a complex function of the API and polymer properties, and the API concentration in the formulation.
the PC SAFT model can predict the phase behavior of amorphous API/polymer systems as a function of water content.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

water absorption is a critical parameter for long term stability of amorphous API formulations, and that the phase behavior of the formulation can be predicted using the thermodynamic PC SAFT model and the Gordon Taylor model.
the PC SAFT model is a powerful tool for the prediction of the phase behavior of amorphous API/polymer systems and the impact of water sorption on this behavior.
the thermodynamic model can be used to predict the effect of absorbed moisture in amorphous API/polymer systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thermodynamic model, PC SAFT, can be used to predict the phase behavior of amorphous formulations in the presence of water.
the thermodynamic model can be used to predict the effect of humidity on the API solubilty in the polymer as a function of the API content in the polymer and the relative humidity.
the phase behavior of amorphous API/polymer systems as a function of RH can be predicted by a combination of PC SAFT and Gordon Taylor equation.
